nodes.summary: For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the algebraic part $X^{\mathrm{alg}}$ of $X$ is the union of all connected, infinite semialgebraic sets $Y$ with $Y \subseteq X$.
nodes.title: Algebraic part of a set

nodes.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be definable in $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$. Then there is a polynomial $f$ in two variables with real coefficients such that the following holds for all natural numbers $g$ and $H$. nodes.title: Wilkie's conjecture for the real exponential field

nodes.summary: For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and natural numbers $g$ and $H$, the set $X(g, H)$ consists of the points $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n) \in X$ whose coordinates are all algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that the field $\mathbb{Q}(x) = \mathbb{Q}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ satisfies $[\mathbb{Q}(x) : \mathbb{Q}] \le g$ and the height $H(x)$ of $x$, the maximum of the absolute multiplicative Weil heights of $x_1, \dots, x_n$…
nodes.title: Points of bounded degree and height

nodes.summary: The function symbols of the language of exponentiation, sorted by arity: there is exactly one, the unary symbol $\exp$, and there are none of any other arity.
nodes.title: Function symbols of the language of exponentiation

nodes.summary: The first-order language whose function symbols are those of the language of rings, namely the binary symbols $+$ and $\cdot$, the unary symbol $-$ and the constants $0$ and $1$, together with the unary symbol $\exp$ of the language of exponentiation; it has no relation symbols.
nodes.title: Language of rings with exponentiation

nodes.summary: The first-order language with a single function symbol, the unary symbol $\exp$, and no relation symbols.
nodes.title: Language of exponentiation

nodes.summary: For $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the height $H(a)$ is the maximum of the absolute multiplicative Weil heights of the coordinates $a_1, \dots, a_n$. A coordinate that is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ counts with height $1$, and for $n = 0$ the height is $0$.
nodes.title: Height of a point

nodes.summary: A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is definable in $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$ if it is definable, with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$, in the real numbers viewed as a structure for the language of rings with exponentiation, where the ring symbols have their usual meaning and $\exp$ is interpreted as the real exponential function.
nodes.title: Definable sets of the real exponential field

nodes.summary: A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is semialgebraic if it is definable, with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$, in the real numbers viewed as a structure for the language of rings.
nodes.title: Semialgebraic set

nodes.summary: For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the transcendental part of $X$ is $X^{\mathrm{trans}} := X \setminus X^{\mathrm{alg}}$, where $X^{\mathrm{alg}}$ is the algebraic part of $X$.
nodes.title: Transcendental part of a set

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
